summary: Codebase Atlas reads a folder of code and draws it three ways. It never runs the code or changes it — it reads the files, works out which ones use which, and turns that into a map you can look around, a diagram of how work flows between the parts, and a plain-English story of what the whole thing does. The story is the only part it cannot work out on its own: somebody writes that down, and Atlas checks it against what it just read.

actors.name: Someone trying to understand a codebase
actors.blurb: A new joiner, a designer, anyone who needs to know how the software fits together.

actors.name: An AI agent
actors.blurb: Reads the same map as JSON instead of looking at it, to answer questions about the code.

actors.name: The desktop app
actors.blurb: The window on a Mac, Windows or Linux machine. The only place that can open a folder from the disk.

actors.name: The command line
actors.blurb: Prints the whole map as JSON, so scripts and agents can read a codebase without a screen.

actors.name: The iPad companion
actors.blurb: An iPad or phone borrowing a computer's eyes over Wi-Fi. It never holds the code itself.

actors.name: The reader
actors.blurb: Walks the folder, skips what git ignores, and measures every file it keeps.

actors.name: The parser
actors.blurb: Actually reads the code to find what each file declares and which other files it uses — no guessing from filenames.

actors.name: The story checker
actors.blurb: Reads the hand-written story and throws out any part that no longer matches the code, saying which.

actors.name: The one description
actors.blurb: Everything learned about the codebase in one shape. Every view and every tool reads this and nothing else.

actors.name: The three views
actors.blurb: The story you land on, the map you fly over, and the flow diagram of what uses what.

actors.name: A folder of code
actors.blurb: Somebody's repository, sitting on a disk. Only ever read, never written to.

actors.name: The hand-written story
actors.blurb: A short account of what the code is for, written by a person or an agent. No parser can work this out.

actors.name: GitHub
actors.blurb: Where public repositories come from when there is no folder on this machine.
